stem: When is the sensitive period for normal visual development in amblyopia?

options.text: The first few years of life

explanation: The sensitive period is the first few years of life. Amblyopia develops when normal visual development is interrupted during this early window, so prompt recognition of amblyogenic eye disease is important.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because normal visual development is most vulnerable in the first few years of life.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the neonatal period alone is too narrow; the sensitive period extends beyond the newborn period.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 8 to 12 years is not the sensitive period for amblyopia development.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because adolescence is well after the main period of visual developmental vulnerability.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because amblyopia occurs during visual development, not after full visual maturity.
